lines.text: the grammar is never just math — it is always also a claim about what counts as growth
Seven presets, one turtle — the grammar is the artist
One rule, one angle, one axiom — a tree grows
The string is the structure — the tree is just one way to read it
Context sensitivity is how real trees grow — the environment is part of the grammar
Watching a tree grow generation by generation teaches more than seeing the final form
Randomness in the parameters, not the rules, is what makes grammar look like nature
Context-Free Grammars visualizer — animated parse trees showing Chomsky hierarchy (regular → context-free → context-sensitive → …
Change the angle from 25° to 90° and the tree becomes a city
Two rules and a turtle — the dungeon writes itself
Competition emerges when grammars share resources — ecology is grammar plus scarcity
A coral is not one tree — it is many grammars growing from the same rock
A tree is eight numbers — change them and you are doing what evolution does
the excavation record was never impersonal. The general intellect has a face here
Gödel as furniture — the limit is not a bug to fix but the shape of the thing
every sufficiently powerful formal system contains true statements it cannot prove
